description: Create, update, and delete Google Calendar events, list calendars and events, respond to invitations, and find times when everyone is free.

tool_signatures.name: Arcade_ListApps
tool_signatures.description: See the apps the current caller can act on and whether they are connected. Returns each app's id, name, connected state, and (when connected) the account it is connected as. Call this to answer "what apps do I have?" or when the caller's connection state may have changed since the session started.

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_CreateEvent
tool_signatures.description:
Create a new event/meeting/sync/meetup in the specified calendar.

Pass `recurrence` to create a repeating event.

recurrence.description: Recurrence rules for a repeating event, in RFC 5545 format. Each entry is an RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE line; a bare rule is automatically prefixed with 'RRULE:'. Examples: ['RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10'] for every Mon/Wed/Fri for 10 occurrences, or ['RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=20241231T000000Z'] for daily until 2024-12-31. Omit for a one-time event.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to create the event in, usually 'primary'.

end_datetime.description: The datetime when the event ends in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-12-31T17:30:00'.

start_datetime.description: The datetime when the event starts in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-12-31T15:30:00'.

add_google_meet.description: Whether to add a Google Meet link to the event. Defaults to False.

attendee_emails.description: The list of attendee emails. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

send_notifications_to_attendees.description: Should attendees be notified by email of the invitation? (none, all, external_only)

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_DeleteEvent
tool_signatures.description: Delete an event from Google Calendar.

event_id.description: The ID of the event to delete

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar containing the event

send_updates.description: Specifies which attendees to notify about the deletion

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_FindTimeSlotsWhenEveryoneIsFree
tool_signatures.description: Provides time slots when everyone is free within a given date range and time boundaries.

end_date.description: The end date to search for time slots in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Defaults to seven days from the start date. It will search until this date at the time 23:59:59.

start_date.description: The start date to search for time slots in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Defaults to today's date. It will search starting from this date at the time 00:00:00.

email_addresses.description: The list of email addresses from people in the same organization domain (apart from the currently logged in user) to search for free time slots. Defaults to None, which will return free time slots for the current user only.

end_time_boundary.description: Will return free slots in any given day until this time in the format 'HH:MM'. Defaults to '18:00', which is a usual business hour end time.

start_time_boundary.description: Will return free slots in any given day starting from this time in the format 'HH:MM'. Defaults to '08:00', which is a usual business hour start time.

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_ListCalendars
tool_signatures.description: List all calendars accessible by the user.

max_results.description: The maximum number of calendars to return. Up to 250 calendars, defaults to 10.

show_hidden.description: Whether to show hidden calendars. Defaults to False

show_deleted.description: Whether to show deleted calendars. Defaults to False

next_page_token.description: The token to retrieve the next page of calendars. Optional.

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_ListEvents
tool_signatures.description:
List events from the specified calendar within the given datetime range.

min_end_datetime serves as the lower bound (exclusive) for an event's end time.
max_start_datetime serves as the upper bound (exclusive) for an event's start time.

For example:
If min_end_datetime is set to 2024-09-15T09:00:00 and max_start_datetime
is set to 2024-09-16T17:00:00, the function will return events that:
1. End after 09:00 on September 15, 2024 (exclusive)
2. Start before 17:00 on September 16, 2024 (exclusive)
This means an event starting at 08:00 on September 15 and
ending at 10:00 on September 15 would be included, but an
event starting at 17:00 on September 16 would not be included.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to list events from

max_results.description: The maximum number of events to return

min_end_datetime.description: Filter by events that end on or after this datetime in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-09-15T09:00:00'.

max_start_datetime.description: Filter by events that start before this datetime in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-09-16T17:00:00'.

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_RespondToEvent
tool_signatures.description:
Accept or decline (RSVP to) a meeting invitation on the authenticated user's behalf.

Sets the user's responseStatus for an event they were invited to.

event_id.description: The ID of the event to respond to. Use the event id from list_events to respond to a single occurrence of a recurring event, or its recurringEventId to respond to the whole series.

response.description: The RSVP response: accepted or declined.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar containing the event

send_updates.description: Should attendees be notified of the response? (none, all, external_only)

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_UpdateEvent
tool_signatures.description:
Update an existing event in the specified calendar with the provided details.
Only the provided fields will be updated; others will remain unchanged.

`updated_start_datetime` and `updated_end_datetime` are
independent and can be provided separately.

event_id.description: The ID of the event to update

updated_summary.description: The updated title of the event

updated_location.description: The updated location of the event

updated_recurrence.description: Updated recurrence rules for a repeating event, in RFC 5545 format. Each entry is an RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE line; a bare rule is automatically prefixed with 'RRULE:'. Provide the full set of rules to replace the event's existing recurrence, e.g. ['RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10'] for every Mon/Wed/Fri for 10 occurrences. Pass an empty list ([]) to REMOVE recurrence and make the event a one-time event. Omit (leave unset) to leave recurrence unchanged.

updated_calendar_id.description: The updated ID of the calendar containing the event.

updated_description.description: The updated description of the event

updated_google_meet.description: Whether to update the Google Meet link to the event. (none, add, remove)

updated_end_datetime.description: The updated datetime that the event ends in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-12-31T17:30:00'.

attendee_emails_to_add.description: The list of attendee emails to add. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

updated_start_datetime.description: The updated datetime that the event starts in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-12-31T15:30:00'.

attendee_emails_to_remove.description: The list of attendee emails to remove. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

send_notifications_to_attendees.description: Should attendees be notified of the update? (none, all, external_only)

tool_signatures.name: GoogleCalendar_WhoAmI
tool_signatures.description:
Get comprehensive user profile and Google Calendar environment information.

This tool provides detailed information about the authenticated user including
their name, email, profile picture, Google Calendar access permissions, and other
important profile details from Google services.
